response.text:
RecSys 2024’s [Does It Look Sequential?](https://github.com/Antondfger/Does-It-Look-Sequential) directly supports controlled order probes: evaluate frozen GRU4Rec on original versus shuffled histories, measuring HR@10/NDCG@10 alongside recommendation-list Jaccard@10. Across 15 datasets, several showed weak sequential structure. Thus, changed recommendations establish order sensitivity; only paired accuracy changes establish whether that sensitivity helps prediction. Results do not establish behavior on these four Amazon categories.

Recurrent-state retention and training signals need separate investigation. The [official GRU4Rec implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/gru4rec) distinguishes session-based modeling from longer user-history modeling, making session assumptions relevant when interpreting retention. [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643), an earlier RecSys paper, demonstrates that changing training-target sampling can improve GRU4Rec: apparent recency preference can reflect supervision as well as recurrent dynamics. Neither hidden-state similarity nor gate values alone demonstrate useful long-term memory.

Recommended diagnostic design, inferred from these findings: compare suffix-only histories of increasing length; remove recent versus equally many older/random interactions; shuffle older prefixes while fixing the recent suffix, then shuffle the suffix while preserving its final item. Remove actual items and repad; skip padding updates in recurrence and read the final nonpadding position, never count−1 for left padding. Reset hidden states between users and replay each perturbed history. Keep targets, candidates and model fixed; report paired HR@10 differences separately from score/rank changes and hidden-state cosine distance. Use repeated perturbation draws and paired user-bootstrap confidence intervals, stratified by category/history length. Prefix removal improving validation accuracy suggests interference from older history, but does not prove those preferences are stale.
